lead.headline: UN mission finds 'reasonable grounds' US committed war crimes in Iran
lead.dek: Panel cites 178 civilian dead in Feb. 28 strikes on a Minab school and Lamerd; White House calls it 'unserious nonsense'
body: A U.N.-commissioned fact-finding mission said Thursday it found "reasonable grounds" to believe the United States committed war crimes in two Feb. 28 airstrikes in Iran that killed at least 178 civilians, including a Tomahawk missile strike on a primary school in the southern city of Minab.

The experts concluded "the building of the school was the intended point of impact" in Minab, where Iranian state media said 168 died, most of them children, AP reported. A second strike scattered tungsten pellets over a sports complex and homes in Lamerd, killing 22, the report said; U.S. Central Command denies striking Lamerd.

White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said the council has "accomplished nothing for human rights while spouting unserious nonsense for decades" and called Iran the only party committing war crimes. The mission, which also accused Iran of crimes against humanity against protesters, presents its findings Monday to the 47-member council in Geneva. The Pentagon has not released its own inquiry.

briefs.headline: Trump withdraws Schroyer as nominee to lead ICE
briefs.summary: The White House pulled ex-Oklahoma trooper Lance Schroyer's nomination Thursday; Sen. Rand Paul had withheld a hearing pending DHS data on civilian deaths.

briefs.headline: Judge gives former Syrian prison chief 60 years for torture
briefs.summary: Samir Ousman Alsheikh, convicted in March of torturing inmates at Syria's Adra Prison from 2005 to 2008, was sentenced Thursday in Los Angeles.

briefs.headline: Stocks rally and oil dips below $100 a day after Fed hike
briefs.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.1% and the Dow 316 points Thursday as the 10-year yield fell to 4.93%; U.S. crude briefly slipped under $100 on hopes of Iran talks.

briefs.headline: Texas Guard F-16 crashes in northern Michigan, pilot ejects
briefs.summary: The Texas jet went down near Grawn in Grand Traverse County before 2 p.m. Thursday on a training flight; a 1-mile hazmat evacuation ended by 9:45 p.m.

briefs.headline: Russia opens 3-day Duma vote with anti-war party barred
briefs.summary: Voting runs Friday to Sunday for the 450-seat State Duma, 11 governors and 39 regional legislatures; Yabloko, the only anti-war party, was barred in August.

briefs.headline: IRGC says it struck Togo-flagged tanker in Hormuz
briefs.summary: The Guards said the vessel made an "illegal passage"; UKMTO said a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile, the fire was put out and the crew is safe.

briefs.headline: Nigeria probes deaths of 37 mining suspects in custody
briefs.summary: They died in a civil defence cell in Minna, Niger state; the corps cited a suspected disease outbreak, and a survivor told AP the cell was packed and airless.

briefs.headline: Philippine school shooting kills 3, including gunman
briefs.summary: Two students and a 16-year-old suspected gunman died Friday in Banga, South Cotabato; eight students were hurt, four critically. The governor said the case was contained.

briefs.headline: Morrisey declares Mason County emergency over levee slide
briefs.summary: A slide near Point Pleasant's levee pipe moved 900 cubic yards of bank to within two feet of a rail line, now closed; the 30-day order began Thursday.

briefs.headline: Records tie new firm to Black Diamond Power before hearing
briefs.summary: WVVA found Black Diamond Utilities formed July 2 at the same Mullens address, its COO the sole director, before Monday's PSC receivership hearing.

briefs.headline: PSC clears $11.4M Olcott waterline after a decade of delays
briefs.summary: The Public Service Commission signed off Thursday to the line serving about 110 Kanawha County homes on private wells; bids go out next month.

briefs.headline: McMahon tours Barboursville career center as a dozen protest
briefs.summary: Education Secretary Linda McMahon toured the Woody Williams Center Thursday, calling federal spending a "failed experiment," as a dozen protested.

regional.item: Hope Gas customers in Milton reported July bills of $670 to over $1,000, which the company Thursday blamed on estimated meter readings.
The sheriff's office broke ground Thursday on $2 million in county-funded upgrades to its training center and firing range at Camp Virgil Tate.
An audit given to Wood County commissioners Thursday put the assessor's office shortfall at about $357,000 and found no theft.

away.item: Village trustees voted last week to adopt an enforcement policy for the short-term rental ordinance, with $100 annual registration due each July 1.

hotspots.item: The Webster County Fair ran Sept. 9-12 at Camp Caesar with its first ATV rodeo alongside the Gambill midway and demolition derby, the Echo reported Monday.
North Topsail Beach hosts a public hearing Tuesday at 6 p.m. on the Army Corps draft impact statement for shore protection at New River Inlet; comments run to Oct. 19.

briefs.headline: TSB says Prince George crash probe could take 450 days
briefs.summary: The Aug. 20 Beech King Air landing on Foothills Boulevard hit four vehicles and killed one person. The board has cited one lost engine so far and has moved into its analysis phase.

briefs.headline: Jamieson runs for Area F seat as Dunphy retires after 18 years
briefs.summary: Gary Jamieson, a 23-year Ferndale-Tabor volunteer firefighter, seeks the Regional District of Fraser-Fort George seat covering Willow River to Tabor Mountain in the Oct. 17 vote.

briefs.headline: B.C. Conservatives say ex-director hired investigator on MLAs
briefs.summary: Party president Mauro Francis told about a dozen people, including four MLAs, that Elaine Allan hired a private investigator with party funds without authorization, CBC reported. Findlay said she had no knowledge of it.

briefs.headline: B.C. adopts PCT as time zone code for year-round daylight time
briefs.summary: Pacific Time, abbreviated PCT, replaces PST and PDT ahead of the first November without a clock change, the citizens' services ministry said Thursday. Manitoba adopted permanent daylight time the same day.

briefs.headline: Carney tells EU Parliament Canada will vote on alliance
briefs.summary: Canadian MPs will debate and vote on the final structure of a Canada-EU alliance, Carney said in Strasbourg Thursday after telling the chamber the two are "not fair-weather allies." A Montreal summit follows Oct. 29-30.

briefs.headline: N.L. House votes 21-18 to advance Churchill River deal
briefs.summary: All 20 Progressive Conservatives and one independent backed the Hydro-Quebec agreement Thursday night; Liberals, NDP and Keith Russell opposed. The Innu Nation asked for a no vote, citing Gull Island payments.

briefs.headline: Two-month HIV shots beat daily pills in African teen trial
briefs.summary: Viral rebound at 96 weeks was 1% on eight-week injections versus 6% on daily tablets among 476 adolescents in four African countries, a UCL-led trial in The Lancet found.

briefs.headline: Genome study names first new wildcat species in a century
briefs.summary: Leopardus tilcayo, a spotted cat about 18 inches long from Bolivia's Yungas near La Paz, was described in Current Biology from whole-genome sequencing of two animals.

briefs.headline: Stanford physicists watch a quantum jump in sound
briefs.summary: A superconducting qubit read a chip-scale resonator that rings for two milliseconds and caught phonons dropping from energy level one to zero, the team reported in Science.

briefs.headline: NASA picks Falcon 9 to launch StarBurst gamma-ray detector
briefs.summary: The Pioneers-program smallsat, built to catch short gamma-ray bursts from neutron star mergers, will fly as a Bandwagon rideshare from Cape Canaveral no earlier than 2028, NASA said Thursday.

briefs.headline: Judge keeps X-Apple settlement terms from OpenAI
briefs.summary: Judge Mark Pittman reviewed the agreement privately and found nothing relevant to X and SpaceXAI's remaining antitrust claims against OpenAI, which got more time to seek summary judgment, 9to5Mac reported.

briefs.headline: Plugin flaw let attackers hijack AI coding agents, firm says
briefs.summary: Security startup Air said its Plugin4Shell bug let a swapped commit pass SHA-pinning in Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, Google's Gemini CLI and Microsoft Copilot; Claude Code and Codex are patched, The Register reported.

briefs.headline: Unsealed filings show Microsoft memo calling AI scraping theft
briefs.summary: A January 2023 memo by Microsoft's Brent Hecht called training-data scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history,' in filings unsealed in The New York Times' suit against OpenAI and Microsoft, TechCrunch reported.

weather_ear: Friday's forecast follows at 7:15, from the weather desk.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers ran no regional line; Russia's Duma vote runs through Sunday, and the U.N. mission presents its report in Geneva on Monday.
